pages.title: Agent and chat subsystem
pages.purpose: How the agent loop works inside a workspace: chat history and message model, proposed-changes materialization and merge, the Code Mode agent (pi-based model routing, executeCode, tool calls, chat bindings), compaction, auto-approval of gatekeeper actions, and agent spawners.
instructions: Cover auto-approval (auto-approvable action kinds) and the agent suspension/resume on awaitDecision actions.
Cover the AI model routing: getModel with three modes (user BYOK gateway, platform gateway, direct provider) and AI Gateway cost log accounting.
Describe the AgentHooks interface that decouples the agent loop (agent.ts) from the overseer (overseer.ts).
Explain chat changes: proposed changes, materialization (materializeChatChanges), three-way merge via git-store, compaction checkpoints.
Explain the Code Mode agent: it writes and executes code snippets; executeCode runs in a sandboxed Dynamic Worker with bindings from prepareChatBindings.
Explain the chat bindings model: named bindings map env names to workpieces (gadgets, gatekeepers, AI models); ambient capsules; validateBindingName.

pages.title: Gadgets, git storage, and blueprints
pages.purpose: The gadget (workspace/workpiece) model, the git object store inside the Overseer, code flow (Yjs history to commits), export formats, and the full blueprint lifecycle: creation, propagation through Gadget DO -> User DO -> KV, R2 content, .gadget archives, bundled format blueprints, and instantiation paths.
instructions: Cover export formats and the Outputs index (syncWorkspaceOutputs).
Cover instantiation paths: newGadgetFromBlueprint (user flow) and the agent's createGadget tool path.
Describe the git object store (git-store.ts): real git loose objects in a typed-storage collection, refless, isomorphic-git plumbing, three-way merge.
Explain blueprints: what they capture, the 3-store propagation (Gadget DO -> User DO -> KV) with dirty flag, R2 content keyed by <id>/<version>, .gadget archive format, import/export.
Explain bundled format blueprints: format-blueprints/ directory, build-format-blueprints.mjs, stable readable IDs, install on first /api request, promotion once.
Explain the workpiece model: a numbered per-workspace id shared across gadgets and gatekeepers, derived facet names.

pages.title: Cloudflare gatekeeper
pages.purpose: The Cloudflare gatekeeper serving three purposes from one OAuth connection: sign-in, AI Gateway billing, and Workers Observability read-only telemetry; its resource granularities, the strict response-validation layering, the worker-scoped filter guarantees, and the billing scopes that fail closed.
instructions: Cover the AI Gateway billing flow: getUsableAccessToken, account selection, balance cache, BYOK routing.
Describe the observability layering: observability-api.ts (only HTTP), observability-parse.ts (validates responses), observability-session.ts (all reads through #observe), observability-discovery.ts.
Explain the three unrelated purposes sharing one OAuth app and how scopes fail closed to BILLING_SCOPES.
Explain the two resource granularities (whole account vs one Worker) both mapping to one indivisible scope; the capability boundary is the binding.
Explain worker-scoped bindings: immutable $metadata.service filter + re-filtering, withholding provider counts, pagination cursor handling, summarizeFilter (no filter values in audit trail).

pages.title: Context Library gatekeeper
pages.purpose: The Context Library: an auto-provisioned gatekeeper providing a per-user read session (agent singleton) and a management UI, with private and public collections, sharing-domain namespacing, the three Durable Objects + KV layout, agent skills/slash commands, and observer tracking strategy C.
instructions: Describe the DO layout: ContextCollectionDurableObject (content), UserLibraryDurableObject (private collections per account), LibraryRegistryDurableObject (public set), plus a KV namespace.
Explain auto-provisioning: GatekeeperVendor.createAccount mints an account per user with no OAuth; describe() declares singleton + providesUi.
Explain observer strategy C over collections (public vs private ownership) via ContextVerifier.
Explain sharing-domain namespacing (binding props) so multiple workshops sharing one gatekeeper instance stay isolated.
Explain the read session (search/list/read) and the ContextLibrary types, agent skills as slash commands, and getAgentCatalog.

pages.title: MCP gatekeepers
pages.purpose: The two MCP gatekeepers (gatekeeper-mcp and gatekeeper-mcp-portal) and their shared library mcp-shared: Streamable HTTP client, trust tiers (byo/vetted), read/action classification, the resource-URL scope grammar, OAuth chain, at-most-once action application, and the many limits.
instructions: Explain the at-most-once guarantee for approved calls (claim-before-send) and the fail-safe classification of uncertain outcomes.
Explain the division of labor: mcp-shared holds shared logic; the connectors keep vendor entrypoints, DO classes, and configurator UI.
Explain the trust tiers and how tool annotations drive read-only classification and auto-approval; nothing outside tools.ts reads annotations.
Note the connectors are owner-only (sharing-policy).
Summarize the scope grammar and the endpoint/host blocklist and sdkFetch requirement.

pages.title: Scheduled Tasks gatekeeper
pages.purpose: The Scheduled Tasks gatekeeper: an auto-provisioned account exposing an ambient singleton for registering persistent workspace callbacks and a read-only management UI; the ScheduleDriver Durable Object's state machine (active/retrying/pending run leases), the shared-alarm delivery loop, quotas, and revocation.
instructions: Cover quotas (500/account, 100/workspace), revoked accounts, and the observability conventions.
Describe the one ScheduleDriver DO per account: storage layout (metadata, schedule:, caps:), the shared alarm, and the delivery loop with ALARM_BATCH_SIZE and concurrency.
Explain run state transitions (active/retrying/pending) and the lease/recovery watchdog; failures close as may-or-may-not-have-fired.
Explain the auto-provisioned account and its singleton session (registering cron-like workspace callbacks) and the management UI.

pages.title: Gatekeeper framework
pages.purpose: The gatekeeper model that gives agents/gadgets sandboxed access to external services: the three-tier Vendor/User/Gatekeeper hierarchy, OAuth account lifecycle, the ApprovalQueue (observations, actions, auto-approval), hooks, the write-gatekeeper skill workflow, and how gatekeepers are installed and bound into workspaces.
instructions: Cover getGatekeeperClassFor as the chokepoint where a resource URL becomes a capability, and GatekeeperUserVerifier/addObserver.
Describe how a gatekeeper is connected: connectAccount callback, connected account records in the User DO, credential expiry notifications, reconnect.
Describe the three-tier hierarchy (GatekeeperVendor WorkerEntrypoint, GatekeeperUser with ctx.props, Gatekeeper DO facet implementing a binding).
Explain action simulation (agents keep working while actions await approval) and auto-approvable action kinds.
Explain hooks (bindHook/startHook/HookController/HookInitiator) and persistent stubs.
Explain the ApprovalQueue contract: authorizeObservation before returning reads, submitAction for side effects that are applied only after applyAction, reject/restart, revert.
Reference the write-gatekeeper skill as the canonical build guide and list reference implementations.

pages.title: Architecture overview
pages.purpose: System-level map of Cloudflare OS: the OS metaphor (kernel/shell/drivers/processes), the Workers runtime model (Durable Objects, Dynamic Workers/Facets, service bindings), the three deployment tiers (router, workshop-backend, gatekeepers), and the core security posture (capability-based access, sandboxing, human-in-the-loop approval).
instructions: Describe the two sandbox layers for gadgets (server Dynamic Worker with internet disabled, client sandboxed iframe with CSP).
Explain the router's role as the public origin and its path-prefix routing, including that routing config IS the binding set.
Explain the runtime model: every workspace is an Overseer Durable Object, each gadget runs in a Dynamic Worker Facet, gatekeepers install facets into workspaces.
Present the OS analogy table (kernel=workshop-backend, drivers=gatekeepers, shell=workshop-frontend, processes=gadgets, executables=blueprints).
State clearly what is established by the source and what is aspirational (e.g. README marketing claims vs code).

pages.title: RPC layer and shared API
pages.purpose: The Cap'n Web RPC layer that connects the SPA, workshop-backend, and gatekeepers: the PublicApi/AuthenticatedApi surface, the gatekeeper three-tier interfaces, @validateRpc runtime validation, promise pipelining, and the stub-disposal/lifecycle conventions every caller must follow.
instructions: Cover the gatekeeper interface hierarchy (GatekeeperVendor WorkerEntrypoint, GatekeeperUser, Gatekeeper DO facet, Session) from workshop-shared/src/gatekeeper.ts.
Cover the stable error-code helpers (codedErrorFamily) and validateBindingName chokepoint.
Describe the PublicApi (unauthenticated) vs AuthenticatedApi (post-authenticate) split and the auth flows (password, Cloudflare Access, gatekeeper sign-in).
Explain how the server's /api endpoint serves both HTTP batch and WebSocket RPC sessions (server.ts).
Explain key conventions: @validateRpc, promise pipelining, stub disposal, useState wrapping stubs in objects (client side).

pages.title: Sharing and observer enforcement
pages.purpose: Collaborator sharing and the observer security model: the permission graph (user/share-link edges, effective-role fixed point), lazy revocation, share keys, the build/use capability split, and observer verification that prevents leaking data a collaborator could not access directly.
instructions: Cover terminate-live-sessions-on-revocation (scheduleRevocationRestart / ctx.abort).
Cover the strategies (A/B/C/D) each gatekeeper resource type uses and where the decision table lives.
Describe the permission graph: edges, computeEffectiveRoles fixed-point, lazy revocation, preview/confirm, keepUsers re-rooting.
Explain the observer model: ObserverConfigCallback on open, account choices, addObserver/removeObserver/getVerifier, excludeObservers forward restriction, observer record lifecycle.
Explain the two sharing mechanisms: collaborators (build/use roles) and share links (HMAC-hashed keys).

pages.title: Workshop backend (kernel)
pages.purpose: The workshop-backend kernel: entry point and routing, the UserDurableObject (accounts, sessions, AI models, connected accounts, blueprints, outputs), AdminSettings/AdminApi (deployment config, formats, featured blueprints), the Overseer Durable Object's role and storage schema, and typed-storage as the persistence layer.
instructions: Cover the capability minting chokepoints: getGatekeeperClassFor (admin-disabled gatekeepers/resources enforced), getAdminApi (isAdmin once), gatekeeper vendor map from GATEKEEPER_* bindings.
Cover the formatted-error code families and the AdminSettings KV mirror consistency model.
Describe the storage schemas: typed-storage collections and singletons for the user DO and overseer; the AdminConfig owned by AdminSettings and mirrored to a reserved KV key.
Explain retryOnDoReset and DO-reset handling for pure reads.
Explain the Durable Object set: UserDurableObject (keyed by email/username), OverseerDurableObject (per workspace), AdminSettings (singleton getByName('')), PendingLogin (transient).
Explain the provisioning policy for auto-provisioned (ambient) gatekeepers (disabled/optional/enabled) and how accounts are minted/persisted.

pages.title: Change guides
pages.purpose: Focused, step-by-step guides for representative maintenance tasks: adding a new gatekeeper, adding a bundled format blueprint, adding an admin-managed setting, changing the shared RPC API, and running/debugging the release pipeline.
instructions: Adding a bundled format blueprint: place the .gadget + .json sidecar, run the build generator, note the install-on-first-request behavior and the never-rename-blueprintId rule.
Adding a gatekeeper: follow the write-gatekeeper skill phases, add the service binding, deploy-inputs.json/wrangler config, and the configurator UI task.
Changing the RPC API: edit workshop-shared/src/api.ts, keep @validateRpc, respect the doc-comment-every-exported-member rule for workshop-shared.
Each guide must be concrete: name the files to touch, the tasks/scripts to run to verify, and the review constraints for the kernel packages.
Mention the release pipeline commands and the golden-file test regeneration (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1).

pages.title: Development workflow and build system
pages.purpose: The repo's development environment and build system: Vite+ tasks and caching (vp run), the dev server generation logic, the frontend dev client, package build/test scripts, environment-variable handling in tasks, and the noEmit/type-check-only build model.
instructions: Cover lint (oxlint via vp lint), types:check, and the single-threaded tsc/tsgo notes.
Explain Vite+ (vp) tasks vs scripts: build is a task (type-check + codegen, noEmit), test is a cached task, caching semantics and the stripped environment (env declarations).
Explain build:app/build:app:dev for gatekeeper UIs, build:configurator, and format-blueprints generation.
Explain the pnpm vs vp distinction (pnpm --filter cannot see tasks) and common pitfalls documented in AGENTS.md.
Explain the two-runner dev setup and the dev-router (no ASSETS binding proxies to backend).

pages.title: Testing infrastructure
pages.purpose: How tests are organized and run: vitest projects (Node vs workerd pools), assert-workerd setup, the per-package test tasks and their caching, the integration-test harness (createTestHarness, fixture gatekeeper, RPC client), and the constraints that shape suites.
instructions: Cover the timeout watchdog (with-timeout.ts) and the memory/OOM caveat for workerd fleets.
Describe the integration test harness in packages/integration-tests: real workers in workerd, Cap'n Web over WebSocket, fixture gatekeeper with an HTTP control route, storage isolation by convention.
Explain how to run tests: pnpm test, pnpm --filter <pkg> test:run, and the difference from the cached vp run test task.
Explain the two vitest projects per package (vitest.config.ts Node vs vitest.worker.config.ts workerd) and assert-workerd.
Note the constraints: no fake timers across processes, worker entry modules may export only classes and handlers, capnweb boundary via rpc-client.

pages.title: Deployment, routing, and release pipeline
pages.purpose: How a Cloudflare OS instance is deployed and updated: the router's routing model, the release manifest contract (build-release/upload-release/promote-release), placeholder templating for customer accounts, the deploy-wizard inputs, and the admin panel's deployment-level settings.
instructions: Describe the release flow: build byte-identical bundles, upload to R2 (content-addressed), promote via manifest copy; candidates vs releases; the golden-file test.

Describe the router: public origin, path-prefix routing (/api and /blueprint-screenshot to backend, /gatekeeper/<name>/* to bound gatekeepers via GATEKEEPER_* scanning, ASSETS for the frontend), email handler.
Explain deploy inputs (DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS, NO_DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS, deploy-inputs.json), preinstall and singleton gatekeepers.
Explain the release manifest: MANIFEST_VERSION, placeholders ($ACCOUNT_ID, $KV_*, $WORKER_NAME(...), $SECRET(...), $PUBLIC_BASE_URL), the closed placeholder list, worker kinds and installability.
Summarize deployment config: env-var-driven auth (AUTH_GATEKEEPERS, DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH, CF_ACCESS_*), admin-config soft settings, backend instance-state vars injected at PUT time.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical, source-grounded guide to running the whole stack locally (pnpm run-local and the pnpm dev-server/dev-client pair), what each command does, what it builds, where data lives, and how to configure OAuth-backed sign-in and AI Gateway in a local .dev.vars.
instructions: Explain what run-dev-server.ts generates at startup: wrangler.dev.jsonc files, gatekeeper service bindings, seeded OAuth credentials, and the format-blueprint module.
Keep it practical and task-oriented; reference the exact script names.
Note where data persists (.wrangler) and that the dev backend seeds an admin user named 'admin'.
Show both ways to run locally: pnpm run-local (single command, built frontend served as static assets) and pnpm dev-server + pnpm dev-client (Vite on :3000, wrangler on :8787).
